_readme: Numbers the scripts read, so a planning decision never depends on a constant retyped into prose. Most were measured, and docs/MEASUREMENTS.md says where; some were chosen rather than measured, and _provenance says which (max_run_minutes, min_path_segments, pane_walk_lease_minutes, memory_floor_gb, memory_clear_gb, worker_relaunch_k, pause_grace_seconds, pause_still_working_seconds). Edit this file to calibrate a different machine or a different application, and re-measure with scripts/fleet-load.mjs and scripts/fleet-retro.mjs rather than guessing. fleet.sh reads the copy beside its own checkout first (../calibration.json from scripts/); only a copy of fleet.sh with no calibration beside it falls back to the installed plugin the host records in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json. So edit the copy you actually run. Values fleet.sh uses in shell arithmetic must be whole numbers of at least 1; anything else is reported and replaced by the built-in default.

_provenance.repo_tasks_per_worker: M16 - measured throughput 2.87 and 4.25 tasks per hour per worker on repo-heavy runs
_provenance.repo_worker_ceiling: M21 - a session with no pane is ~330 MB, so the ceiling is attention rather than memory
_provenance.pane_workers_default: M15 - seven panes carried 104 minutes of driving in a 153 minute run
_provenance.frame_gate_min_fps: M01, M02 - below 60 the pane is blind and everything it returns is fiction
_provenance.budget_multiplier: PULL.md - a worker past twice its budget hands the remainder back
_provenance.fanout_default: M13 - a subagent spends ~45k tokens before it does anything, so a part must be worth a slice of work. Read by a planner rather than by a script: LANES.md applies it.
_provenance.coordinator_handoff_k: operator, 2026-10-06: auto-compaction starts a little past 900 K, so the coordinator asks at 700 K and again at 800 K (the step), leaving room to write STATE.md, stop the workers and print the chips before it. The earlier 300 K was chosen after the 2026-10-05 coordinator reached 510 K at thirty percent of its plan; the operator moved it up because a relaunch costs more than the context it saves below this. fleet.sh ctx and status read it.
_provenance.coordinator_handoff_step_k: How often the warning repeats past the mark, for the coordinator and for a worker. Chosen.
_provenance.worker_relaunch_k: operator, 2026-10-06: the same mark as the coordinator, 700 K, for the same reason (auto-compaction starts a little past 900 K). A repo worker grows 20-30 k per task worked inline and four were compacted near their thirtieth [M30]; the coordinator then retires a queue worker unasked (fleet.sh retire, 1.5.14), and asks the operator once before relaunching a brief or older worker. fleet.sh ctx and contexts read it.
_provenance.pause_grace_seconds: The operator chose it: a paused worker gets this long from its first tool call after the pause to finish the step in hand before the hooks hold it to git, fleet.sh and the wake loop; a worker that never calls is held at four times this long after the PAUSED timestamp. Not a measurement. Read by hooks/run-dir.mjs.
_provenance.pause_still_working_seconds: Chosen: a worker holding a claim with no ack this long after PAUSED is named "still working" by fleet.sh status, so the coordinator can message it by title; before that it is "no ack yet". Long enough for a worker in the middle of a 90-120 s sleep or a build to reach its next call.
_provenance.runaway_log_gb: Chosen after 2026-10-08, when closed chats had left 5 GB of tasks/*.output from interactive python loops: a background command that has written this much output is a loop, not a build. fleet.sh ctx names the file once, for the coordinator to stop its writer.
_provenance.max_run_minutes: A ceiling, not a measurement: comparable tools have documented runs that looped for days and cost thousands. A run past this is a decision to continue, not a default.
_provenance.hook_claim_window_minutes: M03 - the workers that died had claimed within the minute; past ten a quiet claim is long work, and the planner's sweep owns it
_provenance.quiet_interval_seconds: Read by a planner when it arms the watch loop in fleet-wait.md, not by any script here.
_provenance.delegate_past_tasks: M30 - a repo worker's context grows 20-30 k per task worked inline and four workers were compacted near their thirtieth; the first three buy the worktree and the traps, after that fleet.sh next says DELEGATE
_provenance.pane_workers_display_ceiling: Read by a planner, not by a script: BROWSER.md is where the display ceiling is applied.
_provenance.min_path_segments: A path is got wrong at its end - an empty variable, a dirname too many - which turns it into its own parent. Depth is therefore the margin for error, counted in mistakes: C:/wtmerge is one slip from the drive root, <project>/.claude/worktrees/wtA is seven. Four is the floor fleet.sh will delete below. Not a measurement: a chosen floor.
_provenance.root_max_members: A candidate wider than this is a place rather than a defect - a 436 finding backlog offered one 51 wide because they all touched a 5,000 line command file. Read by fleet-gate.mjs cluster.
_provenance.root_common_token_share: A token more than this share of a run's findings mention is the project's vocabulary, not a cause. Without the cut, `forEach` and `playerData` came out as candidate causes on the same backlog. Read by fleet-gate.mjs cluster.
_provenance.pane_walk_lease_minutes: A chosen lease, not a measurement. A pane walk has no heartbeat to refresh, so the lease has to outlast a slow walk: the broker sizes hosts against a flat 20 minutes when no walk has been served yet, and this is that plus room. Read by fleet.sh sweep.
_provenance.memory_floor_gb: Free physical memory below this and `fleet.sh next` hands out no more tasks. Chosen, not measured: the machine this was built on sat at 34.6 GB committed against 31.2 GB physical before a fleet started, and one browser tab holding a heavy page took 1.9 GB of what was left [M34].
_provenance.memory_clear_gb: And it starts again only above this. The gap is hysteresis: with one threshold, every worker held on a single reading claims again on the next, together, on the same memory. Chosen rather than measured.
